bayts.text: To him toward whom it is my duty — and I am no idle crier — (I offer) every year gifts of praise:
a blessing that stands before the peace of the Most High, with the Family, the Companions and every sincere counsellor.
Persevere in praising the one in whom hope is placed, and bless him with a sincere blessing.
For I bless him here, with the Family, the Companions and every righteous one.
My God, bless then without end the Chosen One of radiant face.
My God, bless then him who came loving, beloved, patient, forgiving.
My God, bless then him who appeared God-fearing, pure, a leader, of preponderant weight.
My God, bless then him who guided, obedient, obeyed, inclined to righteousness.
My God, bless then him who was called Beneficent and Effacer (al-Māḥī) of every foulness.
a blessing that holds back affliction and ruin, and draws aspirations unmixed, pure;
a blessing that raises to the attaining of heights, that strengthens minds with sound belief;
a blessing that bestows the best of aspirations, through which the fault of soul and spirit vanishes;
a blessing that shows me his face here, with my own eyes, that my wounded heart may be healed;
a blessing that trains the one who prays, whom the Accursed has called toward a ruinous thing.
I have turned my tongue and my heart together toward the one from whom the best of openings is sought,
toward the Chosen, the Elect, the Selected: I mean the generous one, the Intercessor, the sincere counsellor.
He is the one relied upon, the sufficient one with whom one is content, the guarantor, the protector, the fruitful.
Nurtured and nurturer, messenger, prophet, confidant of God, the one to whom He spoke, the eloquent.
Beautiful of face, pure of intellect, a source of goodness, a refuge for every outcast.
Guarantor of lifting the afflictions of whoever takes refuge in him to guard against sins.
Forbidden to whoever refused his guidance is entry, as a welcomed guest, into Gardens that give rest.
And whoever has not entered his path is awaited by a heavy yoke and a Fire that scorches the face.
We have risen above others with loftiness, since the Chosen One has risen with preponderance.
Persevere in praising the sea of generosity, of copious gifts, and you shall obtain the gains.
Persevere in praising him who has gathered the traits of the noble, by the grace of the Giver.
It does not befit an intelligent (man) to utter wondrous praise for any but the magnanimous (Prophet).
Praise of the generous, lofty Prophet holds back toil, ruin and disgraces.
It purifies a heart seized by harm, and clears away the rust and the rising darkness.
I have praised the generous, munificent Prophet, and I hope through him, forever, not to perish.
I have praised my God Who drew me to the service of the Elect, of (many) openings.
I have praised my God with a praise that fulfils (what is due), with the best increase upon what has been granted me.
I have praised my God Who drew me to the service of the one to be followed, the magnanimous.
I have praised my God with gratitude to Him, for drawing my heart to the love of the sincere counsellor (the Prophet),
to the love of the Messenger, whom I bless forever with a graceful praise.
Be then, my master, for the Khadīm, the lowly one, an intercessor on the Day of toil and of grimacing faces.
Upon you be the peace of Him with Whom I seek an end with a success that gives rest.
